svg.text: S3 DENSE BELTS — the slot coupling
How one motor on the lift drives any of the 13 motor-less belt levels (like the drive of a laser-printer toner cartridge).
hub Ø 30, slot 7 mm · blade 5 × 28 mm

g.text: 1 Passing through and docking (seen along the roller axis)
The lift carries an upright blade.
Each level roller ends in a slotted hub;
the slot is open at both ends.
every slot it passes. When the lift stops,
the blade already sits in that level’s
slot: docked, with no extra motion.
Blade turns → hub turns → belt moves.
docking ± 0.5 mm, checked by a slot sensor
2 One motor moves both belts (side section)
1 : 1 belt drives the rear roller AND the blade
The motor turns the lift belt and, through the blade, the docked level belt at exactly the same
speed, so the box crosses the 10 mm gap between the rollers without slipping or tipping.
3 Detent: a level moves only while the lift is docked
A spring ball clicks into a notch every
half-turn and holds the slot upright.
Lift away: the hub is locked, the level
belt cannot creep, the box stays put.
Lift docked: the blade turns the hub
past the ball, click by click.
no sensor or wire in any level
4 Jam protection: a hub that is not upright
blade on a sprung slide (seen along y)

svg.text: The levels need no motor, wire or sensor: all drive comes from the lift, so the whole column has only 2 motors.
